accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the status of Zero Hour in the Indian Parliament?
o: It is a device borrowed from the British Parliament
It is mentioned in the Rules of Procedure of both Houses
It is an informal parliamentary innovation and is not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure
It is expressly mentioned in the Constitution
accepted.x: Zero Hour is an informal Indian innovation. It is not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure and has been in use since 1962; it was not borrowed from another country.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a formal constitutional or rule-based device from an informal parliamentary practice.
accepted.sec: Zero Hour - timing, notice, duration, origin, Rules status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to Zero Hour in the Rajya Sabha, which of the following statements is correct?
o: It follows Question Hour and has a fixed duration of one hour
It is held only after the day's regular agenda is completed
It is not permitted in the Rajya Sabha
It precedes Question Hour, during which urgent public matters may be raised
accepted.x: In the Rajya Sabha, urgent matters of public importance are raised during the first hour, before Question Hour.
accepted.tq: Separate the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha arrangements instead of applying the Lok Sabha sequence to both Houses.
accepted.sec: Zero Hour - timing, notice, duration, origin, Rules status  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Zero Hour:
1. It has no fixed duration prescribed in the Rules.
2. It continues until the regular business of the day is taken up in the Lok Sabha.
3. A member must give the same prior notice as is required for an ordinary question.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Zero Hour has no fixed duration in the Rules and in the Lok Sabha lasts until the day's regular agenda is taken up. Members do not give the prior notice required for an ordinary question; they intimate the Presiding Officer on the same day.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between same-day intimation for Zero Hour and formal prior notice for questions.
accepted.sec: Zero Hour - timing, notice, duration, origin, Rules status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who decides which members may raise matters during Zero Hour?
accepted.x: Members intimate the Presiding Officer on the same day, and the Presiding Officer decides whom to allow to raise a matter.
accepted.tq: Use the question 'who would do this job?' to identify the authority controlling parliamentary proceedings.
accepted.sec: Zero Hour - timing, notice, duration, origin, Rules status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of matters raised during Zero Hour?
o: The Presiding Officer decides which members may be allowed to raise them
Members may raise them without the prior notice required for a question
Ministers are constitutionally bound to give an immediate reply
They concern urgent matters of public importance
accepted.x: Ministers are not bound to reply to matters raised during Zero Hour. The other features correctly describe the procedure.
accepted.tq: Find the single statement that reverses a procedural limitation.
accepted.sec: Zero Hour - timing, notice, duration, origin, Rules status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: When the Chair issues a direction or an assurance is given in relation to a matter raised during Zero Hour, which institution sends the extract to the concerned Ministry for action?
accepted.x: The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs sends the relevant extract to the concerned Ministry when the Chair issues a direction or an assurance is given.
accepted.tq: Identify the administrative body associated with follow-up action on parliamentary assurances and directions.
accepted.sec: Zero Hour - timing, notice, duration, origin, Rules status  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to a no-confidence motion, consider the following statements:
1. It is expressly mentioned in the Constitution.
2. Its constitutional basis is connected with Article 75(3).
3. It may be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
4. It requires the support of 50 members for leave to be granted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: A no-confidence motion is not expressly mentioned in the Constitution. It flows from Article 75(3), is moved only in the Lok Sabha, and requires the support of 50 members for leave.
accepted.tq: Trap the incorrect constitutional-status statement while checking House, support and Article details separately.
accepted.sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha is moved under which Rule of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business?
accepted.x: A no-confidence motion is moved under Rule 198 of the Rules of Procedure of the Lok Sabha.
accepted.tq: Test precise rule-number recall using nearby numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about a no-confidence motion is correct?
o: Reasons for moving it must necessarily be stated
It can be moved in either House of Parliament
It can be moved only by the Leader of the Opposition
accepted.x: The Speaker exercises discretion in admitting or rejecting a no-confidence motion. Reasons need not be stated, and the motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
accepted.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' test to distinguish the Speaker's procedural role from political roles.
accepted.sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: If a no-confidence motion is passed in the Lok Sabha, what is the constitutional consequence?
o: The Lok Sabha is automatically dissolved
The concerned Minister must resign, while the Council continues
Only the Prime Minister must resign
The entire Council of Ministers must resign
accepted.x: The motion tests the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha. If passed, the whole Council of Ministers must resign.
accepted.tq: Connect the procedural outcome with the constitutional principle of collective responsibility.
accepted.sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The first no-confidence motion against the Union Council of Ministers was moved against Jawaharlal Nehru in 1963 by:
accepted.x: The first no-confidence motion against Jawaharlal Nehru was moved in 1963 by J.B. Kripalani.
accepted.tq: Link the event, year and mover rather than relying on the event alone.
accepted.sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the no-confidence motion moved against the Andhra State ministry in November 1954?
o: It was moved by Gouthu Latchanna and carried by 69 votes to 68
It was moved by Gouthu Latchanna and defeated by 68 votes to 69
It was moved by J.B. Kripalani and defeated by 69 votes to 68
It resulted in the continuation of the Prakasam ministry for five years
accepted.x: Gouthu Latchanna's motion in November 1954 was carried by 69 votes to 68. The Prakasam ministry consequently fell after 13 months.
accepted.tq: Use the vote margin and mover together to avoid swapping a closely related historical instance.
accepted.sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events relating to the Andhra State ministry in chronological order:
A. Prakasam ministry fell by one vote
B. President's Rule ended
C. No-confidence motion moved by Gouthu Latchanna
D. President's Rule was imposed
accepted.x: The motion was moved in November 1954, the Prakasam ministry fell by one vote, President's Rule was imposed on 16 November 1954, and it ended on 27 March 1955.
accepted.tq: Fix the sequence using the dated beginning and end of President's Rule and then place the immediate political events.
accepted.sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The no-confidence motion is regarded as the most powerful weapon of executive accountability because it:
o: permits the Speaker to dismiss individual Ministers
enables the Rajya Sabha to remove the Council of Ministers
enforces the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha
accepted.x: A no-confidence motion directly enforces the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that states the constitutional effect rather than a procedural side-effect.
accepted.sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Question Hour in the Lok Sabha is generally held during:
o: The first hour of every sitting
Only the first sitting of each week
The hour immediately before the day's adjournment
The last hour of every sitting
accepted.x: Question Hour is held during the first hour of every sitting of the Lok Sabha, when Ministers answer questions.
accepted.tq: Test the standard time slot without confusing it with the different Rajya Sabha Zero Hour sequence.
accepted.sec: Question Hour - timing, types of questions, answers, notice  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly matches the type of question with its answer and supplementary-question position?
1. Starred question — Oral answer — Supplementaries allowed
2. Unstarred question — Written answer — Supplementaries not allowed
3. Short-notice question — Oral answer — Supplementaries allowed
4. Question to a private member — Oral or written answer
Which of the above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four matches are correct. Starred and short-notice questions receive oral answers with supplementaries allowed; unstarred questions receive written answers without supplementaries; a question to a private member may receive an oral or written answer.
accepted.tq: Check each row independently, especially the answer mode and supplementary-question rule.
accepted.sec: Question Hour - timing, types of questions, answers, notice  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Question to a private member — Blue paper
accepted.x: A question addressed to a private member is printed on yellow paper, not blue paper. Starred, unstarred and short-notice questions are associated with green, white and light pink paper respectively.
accepted.tq: Use the comparison table to locate the single altered colour designation.
accepted.sec: Question Hour - timing, types of questions, answers, notice  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A short-notice question differs from an ordinary question in that it may be admitted when notice is given:
o: Only on the day of the sitting
At least 15 clear days in advance
accepted.x: A short-notice question is one for which notice is given less than 10 days in advance. Ordinary questions require at least 15 clear days' notice.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two notice thresholds instead of treating all questions alike.
accepted.sec: Question Hour - timing, types of questions, answers, notice  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is considered the most effective method of day-to-day vigilance over the executive?
accepted.x: Question Hour is regarded as the most effective method of day-to-day vigilance over the executive because Ministers are required to answer questions.
accepted.tq: Match the parliamentary device with its principal accountability function.
accepted.sec: Question Hour - timing, types of questions, answers, notice  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the recognised tools of parliamentary control over the executive?
o: Judicial review by the Supreme Court
accepted.x: Judicial review is a constitutional function of the judiciary, not a parliamentary device listed among the tools of legislative control over the executive.
accepted.tq: Separate parliamentary control devices from mechanisms belonging to another constitutional organ.
accepted.sec: Tools of parliamentary control over the executive  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following are tools of parliamentary control over the executive?
1. Question Hour
2. Calling Attention motion
3. Committee system
4. Budget approval
5. Motion of Thanks
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Question Hour, Calling Attention motion, the committee system, budget approval and the Motion of Thanks are all tools of parliamentary control over the executive.
accepted.tq: Recognise a complete list while checking whether the final item has been omitted from the coded options.
accepted.sec: Tools of parliamentary control over the executive  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the devices used by Parliament and State Legislatures for controlling the executive?
o: State Legislatures cannot use Question Hour or motions
Parliament alone uses these devices; State Legislatures use only debates
State Legislatures use the same devices, along with estimates and public accounts committees
State Legislatures use only the no-confidence motion
accepted.x: State Legislatures use the same parliamentary devices for executive control and also use estimates and public accounts committees.
accepted.tq: Test the Union–State comparison by identifying the correct extension rather than an exclusive claim.
accepted.sec: Tools of parliamentary control over the executive  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A member raises an objection that the proceedings of the House are departing from the Rules or the Constitution. Which device is being used?
accepted.x: A point of order is raised when proceedings depart from the Rules or the Constitution. There is no debate on it, and the Presiding Officer gives the ruling.
accepted.tq: Identify the device from the procedural situation rather than from its name alone.
accepted.sec: Point of order, closure, guillotine, yielding the floor  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A point of order is raised when proceedings depart from the Rules or the Constitution.
2. A point of order is itself subject to a regular debate in the House.
3. The Presiding Officer rules on a point of order.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. A point of order is not subject to regular debate; the Presiding Officer rules on it.
accepted.tq: Use the procedural consequence to reject the statement that adds an impermissible debate.
accepted.sec: Point of order, closure, guillotine, yielding the floor  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Simple closure — Only important clauses are debated
Closure by compartments — All pending clauses are voted on when time ends
Kangaroo closure — Only important clauses are debated and the others are taken as passed
Guillotine — Matter is declared sufficiently discussed and put to vote
accepted.x: Under Kangaroo closure, only important clauses are debated and the remaining clauses are taken as passed. Simple closure and guillotine have the meanings given to other options.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among similar closure terms by matching each device with its exact operation.
accepted.sec: Point of order, closure, guillotine, yielding the floor  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In parliamentary procedure, 'closure by compartments' means that:
o: A member gives way to the Chair
All pending clauses are put to vote without discussion at the end of allotted time
Clauses are grouped into parts and debated and voted upon part by part
Only the first clause is debated and all others are rejected
accepted.x: Under closure by compartments, clauses are grouped into parts, with debate and voting taking place part by part.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a structured, part-by-part closure from guillotine and yielding the floor.
accepted.sec: Point of order, closure, guillotine, yielding the floor  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What is meant by 'guillotine' in parliamentary procedure?
o: Only important clauses are selected for debate
All pending clauses are put to vote when the allotted time ends, even if they have not been discussed
The Presiding Officer terminates the membership of a disorderly member
The House adjourns without taking a vote
accepted.x: Guillotine refers to putting all pending clauses to vote when the allotted time expires, including clauses that have not been discussed.
accepted.tq: Use the time-limit clue and distinguish automatic voting from selective debate.
accepted.sec: Point of order, closure, guillotine, yielding the floor  [APPSC]

accepted.s: When a member who is speaking gives way to another member or to the Chair, the procedure is known as:
accepted.x: Yielding the floor occurs when the member speaking gives way to another member or to the Chair.
accepted.tq: Match the ordinary procedural action with its precise parliamentary term.
accepted.sec: Point of order, closure, guillotine, yielding the floor  [APPSC]
